items.title: Top 30 API Documentation Interview Questions and Answers
items.summary:
* **Title:** API Documentation Interview: Key Areas – From Basic Concepts to Full-Process Integration

* **Summary:** This article outlines 30 frequently asked questions in API documentation interviews, covering topics such as endpoint definition, differences between HTTP methods, authentication mechanisms (API Key/Bearer/OAuth), parameter parsing, and security best practices. It highlights common integration pitfalls like hardcoding keys, ignoring status codes, and failing to handle pagination, and provides a 12-step verification checklist to help developers build robust API interaction logic.

items.title: Top 25 Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) Interview Questions and Answers
items.summary:
* **Title:** FDE Interview Core Capabilities and Architectural Design Framework for Enterprise-Level AI Systems

* **Summary:** This article outlines the key questions for interviews related to enterprise-level AI systems, covering RAG pipeline security design, multi-dimensional evaluation of AI systems, end-to-end project retrospectives, and strategies for deploying high-risk agents, including the conversion of ambiguous business questions. The article emphasizes that FDE (FDE) needs technical depth, customer discovery, ownership of deployment, and cross-role communication, and proposes a decision framework: “first understand the customer’s problem, then design the architecture.”

items.title: RetroREPLAY: A C++ Program Built to Cure Gamer Decision Paralysis
items.summary:
**Title:** RetroREPLAY: C++ “Retro Game Decision Paralysis” Solution

**Summary:** Developers have created a local desktop “command center” built in C++, designed to address decision fatigue associated with managing retro game collections. The application utilizes Dear ImGui and OpenGL3 for high-performance rendering, employs a dirty marking mechanism for optimized data persistence, and integrates asynchronous threads for handling external API requests. This allows users to maintain data locally while assisting in developing game strategies.

items.title: How Artificial Intelligence Is Transforming Education
items.summary:
**Title:** AI Reshapes Education: Personalization Alongside Challenges to Academic Integrity

**Summary:** Artificial intelligence is significantly improving both the efficiency and accessibility of education through personalized learning paths, 24/7 tutoring, and administrative support. However, the widespread use of AI has also raised serious challenges related to academic integrity, the decline of critical thinking, data privacy, and the digital divide. The future of education will likely involve human-AI collaboration, with the core focus on utilizing AI to enhance, rather than replace, the role of educators.

items.title: 💎 [Exclusive for Members] Outliers, Leverage, and Influential Points Explained: How They Impact Your Regression Model and…
items.summary:
* **Title:** Three Types of Outliers in Regression Models: Outliers, Leverage Points, and Influence Points

* **Summary:** In regression analysis, outliers, leverage points, and influence points are often treated as the same thing, but they have distinct definitions. Outliers are characterized by large residuals, leverage points occur at the edges of the predictor space, and influence points significantly alter model parameters. The recommended approach is to follow a “diagnose and then remove” strategy, using metrics such as residual analysis, leverage values, and Cook distances to identify anomalies, and avoid blindly removing data to preserve genuine business insights.

items.title: Sterling Cooper Built Your UX Process. We Need To Redefine It In The Age of AI And Systems.
items.summary:
* **Title:** Redefining UX Processes: From the “Sterling Cooper” Legacy to Value Delivery in the Age of AI

* **Summary:** The article argues that the “Sterling Cooper” model – established in the 1960s advertising industry (such as Pitch Rooms and an Authorial system) – has become outdated in the age of generative AI. Current UX teams are facing challenges of “loss of institutional memory” and “lack of continuous discovery,” leading to research becoming a one-off delivery rather than a continuous habit, and preventing organizations from accumulating genuine user insights. The article advocates moving away from blindly adhering to past formats, and instead focusing on continuous discovery and internal collaboration, driven by measurable business outcomes. In the age of AI, the value of UX should be demonstrated through solving real problems and long-term organizational learning, rather than simply focusing on “showcasing” and “delivering.”

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation from First Principles
items.summary:
* **Title:** Analyzing the RAG Architecture: Industrial-Grade Solutions for Reducing Hallucinations and Integrating Private Data

* **Summary:** The Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture addresses three key challenges: hallucinations in large language models, knowledge cutoff issues, and access to private data. RAG combines external knowledge bases with Large Language Models through a “retrieve - enhance - generate” process. Its standard pipeline includes four stages: indexing, retrieval, enhancement, and generation, utilizing embedding vectors and Top-k retrieval mechanisms to ensure factual accuracy while enabling dynamic knowledge injection.

items.title: Artigo 1: LLMs e Context Engineering
items.summary:
* **Title:** LLM Context Engineering: From Probability Prediction to Dynamic Information Management – The Underlying Logic

* **Summary:** Large Language Models don’t simply rely on memorization; instead, they predict the next token based on probability. Their core capability relies on the attention mechanism within the Transformer architecture, which dynamically allocates weights to focus on key information. However, context windows have a physical limit, and excessive information can dilute effective signals. Therefore, the key to context engineering involves separating “model behavior adjustment” from “information preparation strategies,” utilizing techniques like Embeddings to precisely retrieve relevant segments, rather than simply adding data.

items.title: The Do-It-Yourself Path to Becoming a Mid-Level Web3 Developer
items.summary:
* **Title:** Web3 Job Market Challenges: Senior Roles Dominate – How Mid-Level Developers Can Overcome the Obstacles

* **Summary:** The Web3 recruitment market in 2026 shows a strong preference for senior roles, with entry-level positions accounting for only 5.2%. Rising AI costs and a return of layoffs are further increasing industry uncertainty. For mid-level developers, recommendations include disabling IDE code completion, requiring AI to explain its reasoning, and encouraging independent coding and debugging, utilizing AI as a mentor rather than a replacement, to rapidly build intermediate skills and pursue senior positions.

items.title: 💎 [Exclusive for Members] I Built an AI Agent to Help Grow My Business on Reddit.
items.summary:
* **Title:** Reddit Authority Agent: From Personal Pain Points to Automated Community Management
* **Summary:** The author, who is a user of GLP-1 medications and a former chef, has developed a Reddit agent for GLP Food Score and Glispy. This agent is not designed for mass link promotion, but instead focuses on monitoring communities, answering genuine questions, and building trust, all while operating within compliance guidelines to support business growth.

items.title: Prompt Engineering Part2: Prompting Strategies and Techniques
items.summary:
* **Title:** Prompt Engineering Part 2: Five Elements for Building Effective Prompts and Output Control Techniques

* **Summary:** This article delves into advanced prompt engineering strategies, focusing on three key characteristics: clarity, specificity, and openness. It explores five elements – instructions, role setting, output format, quotation marks, and delimiters – for precisely controlling LLM responses using Markdown syntax and punctuation. The article emphasizes a complete practice path, ranging from basic instructions to complex reasoning (such as the chain-of-thought method), aiming to improve the accuracy and evaluability of human-machine interaction.

items.title: A Game Developer’s Approach to BIM
items.summary:
* **Title:** Optimizing BIM Rendering Performance with Game Engine Techniques
* **Summary:** Developers have addressed the issue of large BIM model data and slow rendering performance by leveraging game development techniques. Specifically, they utilized Level of Detail (LOD) control, Draw Call optimization, Batching, and Instancing to achieve 60 FPS smooth rendering of an 800MB 3D model within a browser. This solution effectively tackles the performance bottlenecks experienced in traditional BIM tools, offering a viable path for lightweight and cross-platform data visualization.

items.title: BUILDING A SELF-HEALING DATA PIPELINE
items.summary:
**Title:** Building Self-Healing Data Pipelines: AI-Driven Automation for Repair and GitOps Secure Releases

**Summary:** Addressing the frequent crashes of data pipelines in modern data stacks due to schema drift, this project utilizes LangGraph and a ReAct agent, combined with dbt and GitOps, to achieve automated diagnosis, SQL reconstruction, and testing validation. By incorporating a human review process, fixes are submitted only through Pull Requests, significantly reducing operational costs while ensuring the security of enterprise-level production environments.

items.title: I Thought I Knew Pandas… Until I Worked With Real Data
items.summary:
* **Title:** Pandas Masterclass: Moving from “How to Clean” to “Why” – A Shift in Thinking

* **Summary:** Developers working with real-world data have come to recognize that Pandas’ core value lies not just in the function calls themselves, but in questioning the data source and validating business logic. By investigating the meaning of missing values, the causes of duplicate records, and changes in row counts after merging, the author emphasizes a “ask business questions first, then write code” analytical approach. They point out that blindly cleaning data or relying solely on code output without validating the logic leads to drawing seemingly correct, but ultimately incorrect, conclusions.

items.title: Updated Analysis on the 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh War
items.summary:
* **Title:** 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh War Has Not Significantly Impacted the Armenian Economy

* **Summary:** A study utilizing synthetic control methods, comparing the GDP of Armenia with a synthetic Armenia, found that the war had not significantly impacted the economy. Despite incorporating variables such as net migration, current account balances, and military spending, the gap widened to -3.3% in 2021, but this difference remained statistically insignificant. The economic growth observed in 2022 was primarily driven by capital inflows from Russia resulting from the Russia-Ukraine conflict, and was not directly linked to the Nagorno-Karabakh war.

items.title: How Large Language Models Actually Learn
items.summary:
* **Title:** Analyzing the Learning Mechanisms of Large Language Models: From Data to Parameter Optimization

* **Summary:** Modern large language models don't rely on memorizing rules or storing facts; instead, they are built on the Transformer architecture and trained using massive amounts of text data. The models convert text into numerical sequences (Tokenization), predicting the next token and calculating a loss function to dynamically adjust billions of parameters, thereby capturing grammar, semantics, and contextual relationships. The core mechanism involves a “predict - error - optimize” closed loop, resulting in an intelligent system capable of handling complex language patterns and reasoning.

items.title: 💎[Exclusive for Members] Tutorial 15: Debugging GPT Training
items.summary:
* **Title:** GPT Training Debugging: A Systematic Process from Data Pipelines to Generation Quality

* **Summary:** This article establishes a systematic debugging process for GPT training, addressing the issue of “program running correctly but model errors.” The process covers everything from the environment and files to the tokenizer and generation quality. By identifying failures across three categories – correctness, numerical issues, and optimization – and emphasizing the principle of “first verifying the data pipeline before optimizing generation quality,” developers can avoid making blind adjustments to hyperparameters and achieve precise identification and correction.

items.title: NetBSD and My Life (2005)
items.summary:
* **Title:** Mastering NetBSD: From Frequent Failures to Stable and Efficient – The Story of a Network Administrator

* **Summary:** A network administrator at a large UK company, Gary Rolland, experienced frequent Windows server outages, leading to business disruptions and personal difficulties. After testing NetBSD, his team successfully migrated 29 high-load servers to NetBSD 2.0.2, achieving an average daily data processing volume of over 870GB and a significant reduction in failure rates. This migration not only improved system stability but also eliminated the need for weekend on-call shifts, enabling a better work-life balance.

items.title: Show HN: Make your logo extra bright on HDR screens
items.summary:
* **Title:** Utilizing HDR Gain Maps to Enhance Logo Display, Creating Visual Differentiation for LinkedIn
* **Summary:** Developers have created a browser tool, built using Claude Code, to address the issue of low brightness for logos on HDR screens (such as the new MacBook Pro) on platforms like LinkedIn. The tool works by adding gain maps to existing JPEG images, resulting in a visually prominent display of logos specifically on HDR devices.

items.title: Why your local LLM feels dumber than it is
items.summary:
* **Title:** Bottlenecks in Local LLM Performance: Hardware Differences and the Hidden Costs of Sampling Strategies
* **Summary:** Local deployments of Large Language Models often underperform compared to expectations. This is due to calculation discrepancies caused by differences in hardware instruction sets and improper configuration of sampling parameters. Using KL divergence analysis allows quantification of the deviation between the output distribution and a benchmark, revealing a decline in inference quality not due to the model’s weights themselves. It is recommended to use standardized benchmark testing and professional sampling configurations to avoid misjudging system performance based solely on zero-shot testing.

items.title: Scrap
items.summary:
* **Title:** Moxie Marlinspike’s Recollection: A Life in Pittsburgh – “Scrap Metal” and a Philosophy of Survival
* **Summary:** After moving to Pittsburgh in 2006, Moxie Marlinspike faced a period of hardship due to his shattered romanticized vision of winter. Without heating, he relied on a local “scrap metal” team to earn a living by moving old bathtubs and other metal scrap. This experience revealed the raw reality of life in the city’s underbelly and resonated with the tech community’s interest in “hardcore survival” and “resource recycling.”

items.title: A Friendly Introduction to Racket
items.summary:
* **Title:** Racket Language Guide: Building Metaprogramming Capabilities with Macro Expansion
* **Summary:** Racket, a modern branch of the Lisp family, utilizes “Homoiconicity” – the ability to treat code as data – and allows users to define custom syntax extensions. The article covers the language’s evolution and the installation of the DrRacket environment, focusing on how to build capabilities like loops, recursion, and graphical drawing using macros (specifically, `define-syntax-rule`). It highlights Racket’s role as a “language for building languages.”

items.title: Show HN: Public Muscriptor Instance (latest, most powerful Audio-to-MIDI model)
items.summary:
* **Title:** Open-Source Audio to MIDI Model Released: GPU-Driven Conversion of Any Song into Piano Music
* **Summary:** Developers have released a public Muscriptor instance, providing a GPU-based audio-to-MIDI model that enables real-time conversion of any song into piano notation.

items.title: Show HN: terminal-code – VS Code inside the terminal
items.summary:
* **Title:** `tode` – VS Code Tool Embedded in Terminals – Released, Supporting SSH Remote Access and Multi-File Comparison

* **Summary:** The open-source tool `tode` integrates the `code-server` and `terminal-browser` to bring the VS Code environment into a terminal. It supports SSH remote connections, file navigation, differential comparison, and shortcut conflict resolution, providing developers with a lightweight, no-GUI code editing solution.
